mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for ≥3 consecutive months
regime_hint: Rising inflationary bias in the Fed’s policy framework
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified tightening period (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not remain above 5.25% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2.5%, it indicates accelerating inflation, prompting the market to discount future earnings more aggressively and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05) during the month of the CPIAUCSL shock, or ΔCPIAUCSL ≤ +2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% month-over-month AND UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative or flat despite the labor indicators meeting the trigger condition (p-value > 0.05 in a rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average, while not accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer demand proxies (e.g., HOUST), predicts a supply-side shock that compresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >3% from its 12-month MA and HOUST does not fall by >5% in the same period
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant during the identified contraction (t-test p < 0.05), or INDPRO recovers without a corresponding decline in demand.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales (not directly available in the catalog; proxy via RSAFS) exceeding +5% for two consecutive months, in the absence of a monetary tightening signal (FEDFUNDS), is interpreted as resilient consumer demand and predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by >5% month-over-month for two consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS ≤ 4.5% in both months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive during the demand expansion (p-value > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% during the same window.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 4.0%, it indicates a sustained easing bias that lowers real rates and increases the present value of future equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days (always-on signal).
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive during the identified easing window (p-value > 0.05), or 3-month FEDFUNDS MA does not fall below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden, unanticipated spike in job openings (proxy via indirect labor demand signals such as PAYEMS growth exceeding +15% in a month) combined with a decline in unemployment (UNRATE) suggests strong labor absorption, which can fuel consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >15% in month t AND UNRATE falls by >0.3 percentage points in month t
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not positive during the trigger month (p-value > 0.05), or UNRATE does not fall as predicted.

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) in two consecutive months, without a corresponding rise in consumer demand (HOUST), is interpreted as a supply-side weakness that reduces earnings expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >4% in month t AND again in month t+1 AND HOUST does not rise by >3% in either month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant during the double contraction (p-value < 0.05), or demand recovers strongly without a second INDPRO contraction.
